brief:
The person tagged the bot in a reply. The post they tagged it in says:
@buildthis.bisks.net keep building!

The thread it's replying to, oldest first (this is the context "this" refers to):
@gracekind.net: I swear the universe created 2006-era Yudkowsky to torture me specifically
  [quoting @gracekind.net: This is not a rejection of empiricism- it’s an argument for favoring simpler theories when the experimental evidence is identical.]
@gracekind.net: “Here’s a guy who says generally reasonable things in the most smug and irritating way possible, have fun defending him”
@tvanl.bsky.social: Is it not then incumbent on someone to rewrite the arguments simply and clearly? LessSmug
@gracekind.net: This is actually not a bad idea
@yhjet.bsky.social: many of the 'background' ideas in the sequences (esp. wrt materialism, phil-of-lang, phil-of-mind, metaethics) were previously invented elsewhere and my desire to read/endorse/defend EY thought really deflated after I had read more academic philosophy
@yhjet.bsky.social: the sequences do reference heuristics & biases concepts and papers but are pretty poor about providing references for other topics, especially philosophy (aside from a few references to Dennett and Parfit). unclear whether this was deliberate or EY was simply not familiar
@yhjet.bsky.social: the 'human's guide to words' sequence is especially frustrating because it articulates the imo basically correct distillation of some core debates in phil-of-lang but doesn't refer the existing concepts there (natural kinds, new riddle of induction, implicature, psychological essentialism...)
@gracekind.net: Yep totally, I’ve had similar experiences. A lot of reinventing the wheel / apparent ignorance of prior work
@algon-33.bsky.social: No, I'm pretty sure EY learnt all this stuff from elsewhere and didn't invent much of it e.g. the map territory thing he (indirectly) got from general semantics, the stuff about the nature of truth he got from Pierce etc.
@algon-33.bsky.social: I reckon he was just too lazy to cite everything as fussily as an academic because: a) he was posting things daily b) he is not an academic, he's a blogger.

That's not to say he did no citations. But they certainly weren't enough to trace down all the sources of the ideas in the Sequences.
@norvid-studies.bsky.social: mm that's a justification of not citing chapter and verse on a daily post but some kind of "btw I imported this root and branch from pierce" is free, known (to the author) and aura-deflating to the reader so it's kind of obvious which path yud's brain is gonna galtonboard carom down, actionspacewise
@norvid-studies.bsky.social: in cases where he did want to cite influences, he made sure to commensurately inflate their aura to studiously follow an aura-conservation law; the phrase "1000 year old vampire" was used at some point,
@yhjet.bsky.social: I'm not necessarily accusing EY of this wrt Jaynes but another common trick in this space is citing an extremely thick tome that realistically the audience isn't going to read. Jaynes' PT:TLoS is after all a graduate textbook
@gracekind.net: I’m not familiar with this work so I’ll guess at the acronym, is it “physical therapy: the life of stretch”?
@yhjet.bsky.social: lmao that is what you need in order to lift it up but no it's Probability Theory: The Logic of Science

it's been ~15 years but I remember it being very dense and very didactic, lots of strongly-worded claims about epistemology. definitely a major influence on the EY house style
@yhjet.bsky.social: hmm actually Jaynes might be the one place where the sequences do properly acknowledge their influences, but as norvid says above the aura projection here feels...misaligned with the experience of reading the actual source material (ime)
